Agents’ Last Exam

paper.arxiv.2606.05405

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2606.05405v4. Task-workflow versus task-instance methods and living private/public inventory limits establish benchmark construction. Preserve150/152scope ambiguity and no supporter-to-source contribution inference. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The release figure reports 150 public, 1017 private and 323 unverified instances out of 1490; later text describes a 152-task public set while the executed-inventory appendix says 150. This unresolved version/count discrepancy and workflow-versus-instance distinction must remain explicit rather than silently treated as one complete reviewed denominator.

repair.qualbinding.20261111.v2.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2606.05405.limitation

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • Domain practitioners submit workflows through an AI-assisted portal; engineers implement environments/graders and an expert committee checks reference correctness, context and evaluation tolerances.
  • A task workflow differs from a runnable instance. Figure 5 splits 1,490 instances into 960 external-submission variants and 530 commissioned instances, with 150 public, 1,017 private and 323 unverified.
  • Main text describes 152 public tasks, while Figure 5 and Appendix B.3.2 report 150. The conclusion calls 960 task workflows; this is retained as a distinct source label rather than silently equated with external-submission variants.
  • Code-based checking is the default, but selected visual/free-text workflows use targeted LLM probes. Static analysis of the open reference workflow tree reports 93.2% code-based and 6.8% LLM-judged workflow share, not global runtime or instance percentages.
  • The thirteen-domain/fifty-five-subdomain taxonomy is SOC/O*NET-grounded, and prior-benchmark mapping uses an LLM-assisted classifier. Table 1 labels tier sizes 67, 55 and 38 (sum 160), while the paper separately reports 150 or 152 public tasks. The read contexts do not reconcile these denominators or establish whether tiers overlap; no overlap is inferred. Only a subset of configurations has three repeated runs.
  • This repair does not infer labor-market representativeness, GDP impact or a supplier-contribution edge from domain coverage or financial acknowledgments.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

ALE separates a task workflow from runnable task instances and implements load/start/evaluate interfaces over expert-provided artifacts and references. Expert/engineering QC and code-based checks are the default, but selected visual/free-text workflows still use targeted LLM probes; static grader-type percentages refer to the open reference workflow tree, not all 1490 inventory instances.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

In Table 1’s 67-instance Near-Term tier, the Codex/GPT5.5 row reports 38.1% full-pass and 64.7% mean score. Full-pass and fractional-score metrics are distinct, and repeated runs cover only a subset of configurations; these reported values do not establish universal professional-work success or economic output.
